claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CEO Ted Pick said investments in the self-directed and Workplace channels drive Wealth Management's differentiated client acquisition funnel. He said the firm reaches over 19 million relationships and added net new assets of over $250 billion in each of the past two years, on track to $10 trillion plus of total client assets.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Pick said Wealth has three channels (financial advisors, Workplace and E*TRADE), each a category leader, which together make up the firm's 'strategic client acquisition model'. He said Wealth Management had net new assets of over $350 billion last year and, over five years, $1.6 trillion plus of net new assets with a doubling of fee-based flows. The 2025 10-K reports 2025 net new assets of $356 billion.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), management said its intentional strategy is to introduce and educate retail clients on the value of advice. Management cited the EquityZen acquisition, an expanded Carta partnership and a Zero Hash collaboration as foundations for 'sustainable growth to widen our competitive moats'.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Pick said the client acquisition funnel will continue to drive Wealth Management's performance. He said the firm seeks, 'with the passage of time', to grow stand-alone wealth assets from the current $8 trillion to $10 trillion. CFO Sharon Yeshaya credited 'sustained investments in our client acquisition funnel' with reaching more clients and deepening existing relationships.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Pick described the 'integrated scaling of the funnel' as a critical strategic matter. He listed the self-directed channel, a differentiated and expanding workplace offering, and trust-based relationships between financial advisers and clients, with technology as a differentiator.

Workplace (1Q25 call, April 2025): Yeshaya said an incremental $20 billion migrated from workplace to the advisor-led channel in the quarter, adding to roughly $300 billion accumulated since the channel was expanded in 2020.

Workplace (2Q25 call, July 2025): Yeshaya said 70% of the flows that originate from workplace are net new assets to the firm. She also said workplace-originated flows were running ahead of the roughly $16 billion per year previously cited.

Workplace (3Q25 call, October 2025): Yeshaya said workplace is 'probably the most exciting part' and that the firm is 'just scratching the surface'. She said IPO-driven assets arrive in self-directed accounts and also move directly into advisor-led accounts.

Workplace (4Q25 call, January 2026): management said advisor-led assets originating from workplace and E*TRADE relationships grew to a record $99 billion for the full year, against historical averages of around $60 billion per year.

Workplace (2Q26 call, July 2026): Pick said the record $148 billion of net new assets was driven by large IPOs of late-stage private workplace clients, which he called a cornerstone of the client acquisition funnel. Yeshaya said stock plan IPO flows were just over half of NNA.

Workplace (3Q26 call, October 2026): Yeshaya said fee-based flows of $80 billion included a corporate retirement mandate that supplied nearly half. She said the firm continues to expand its retirement capabilities and deepen engagement with plan participants.

Financial advisor productivity and recruiting (1Q25 call, April 2025): Yeshaya said Q1 net new assets were supported by advisor-led clients, stock plan vesting, 'positive recruiting trends' and self-directed clients. Pick said that at the top of the funnel it is about the financial advisor, citing the firm's access to intellectual capital, technology and compensation viewed as fair. He said the firm is selective but gets a lot of inbound inquiry.

Financial advisor productivity and recruiting (2Q25 call, July 2025): Yeshaya said advisor-led flows were particularly strong. She said they came from new advisors attracted by the strength of workplace, as well as from assets that originated in workplace. Advisor-led flows also came from existing advisors and recruits.

Financial advisor productivity (4Q25 call, January 2026): Pick said the firm is using its scale to broaden advisor capabilities that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending. He said $100 billion migrated to financial advisors in 2025.

E*TRADE / self-directed (2Q25 call, July 2025): Yeshaya said self-directed flows improved year over year, which she credited to investments in marketing and business development and new tools such as E*TRADE Pro. On the 3Q25 call (October 2025) she said the firm was increasing marketing and business development in self-directed. Pick said on the 1Q25 call that the firm is investing in E*TRADE.
claims.source_label: MS transcript 2025-06-30 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-03-31 [IR]

claims.text: Referrals from Institutional Securities and the integrated firm (3Q25 call, October 2025): Yeshaya said workplace and IPO activity are ways to build out the integrated firm. She said the firm has people to shepherd individuals across institutional securities and underwriting, and that there is 'a lot more to go'.

Referrals from Institutional Securities and the integrated firm (4Q25 call, January 2026): management said Q4 net new assets of $122 billion had contributions across all channels. Growth was 'supported by institutional relationships related to the integrated firm'.

Referrals from Institutional Securities and the integrated firm (2Q26 call, July 2026): Pick said that with institutional activity strong and IPO markets open, the firm 'connected the Integrated Firm to translate institutional strength into client value through our adviser-led and E*TRADE channels'. He said the firm led landmark IPOs in the quarter.

Net new assets were $251.7 billion in FY2024 and $356.3 billion in FY2025. Fee-based asset flows were $123.1 billion in FY2024 and $160.1 billion in FY2025. Quarterly net new assets for 4Q25 were $122.3 billion against $56.5 billion in 4Q24.

Management's 2025 quarterly commentary: 1Q25 net new assets were $94 billion, a 6% annualized growth rate of beginning-period assets (April 2025 call). 2Q25 net new assets were $59 billion, strong despite higher seasonal tax payments (July 2025 call). 3Q25 net new assets were $81 billion, with all three channels contributing and the reopening of the IPO market supporting results (October 2025 call).
claims.source_label: MS transcript 2025-03-31 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-06-30 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]

claims.text: 2026 results: net new assets were $118 billion in 1Q26 and a record $148 billion in 2Q26, of which just over half represented IPO-related inflows in the Workplace channel. They were a record $232 billion in 3Q26, again with just over half associated with IPO-related flows. In the first nine months of 2026, management said it delivered roughly $0.5 trillion of net new assets and about $175 billion in fee-based flows.
claims.source_label: MS transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]; MS press - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30 [filing]; MS transcript 2026-09-30 [IR]

claims.text: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Yeshaya said an active IPO calendar accelerates the pace of the funnel. She cautioned that 'flows will fluctuate as lockups expire, funds make distributions and individuals use assets for consumption'. She said the pipeline and connectivity across channels let the firm build relationships early and deepen them over time.

The stated asset goals are $10 trillion plus of total client assets, cited on the 4Q24 call (January 2025). On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Pick said total client assets across Wealth and Investment Management had reached $10 trillion. He also said the firm seeks to grow stand-alone wealth assets from $8 trillion to $10 trillion. These are asset-level goals, not annual NNA targets.

Management's own caution on drivers: the 2025 10-K says NNA is influenced by macro factors, seasonality, the firm's ability to attract and retain financial advisors and clients, capital market and corporate activities, and large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows. It adds that 'should these factors continue, the growth rate of our NNA may be impacted.' The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) repeats this and adds single large client events.
claims.source_label: MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Seasonal tax outflows: on the 2Q25 call (July 2025), management said Q2 net new assets of $59 billion were inclusive of a $22 billion headwind from tax outflows.

Client cash and deposit pricing: the 10-Qs for 2Q25 (August 2025) and 2Q26 (August 2026) say interest rate changes and other macroeconomic factors have affected client preferences, including cash allocation to other products. They also cite 'pricing changes to certain deposit types due to various competitive dynamics', which have affected net interest income. The 2Q26 filing says net interest income may be affected in future periods if these factors persist.
claims.source_label: MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2025-06-30 [filing]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Cash sweep (1Q26 call, April 2026): Yeshaya said sweep balances have behaved with some yield-seeking behavior, and that the transactional nature of the cash is what 'you've seen bottom out' in the near term.

Competition and market risk (2025 10-K, February 2026): the firm lists commercial banks, global investment banks, regional banks, broker-dealers, private banks, registered investment advisers, digital investing platforms, asset managers and fintechs as competitors. It says it competes to attract and retain qualified employees. It also says unfavorable market or economic conditions could affect net new asset flows and flows into fee-based assets, which could hurt Wealth Management results.

gaps.what: No explicit annual or quarterly net-new-asset target or numeric growth-rate goal for Wealth Management was found. The stated goals are asset-level ($10 trillion plus total client assets; stand-alone wealth assets from $8 trillion to $10 trillion).
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley investor day or strategic update presentation, or management commentary on firm-wide Wealth Management goals

gaps.what: The effect of cash sweep or client cash behavior, or competitive deposit pricing, on net new assets is not quantified. The evidence addresses net interest income and sweep balances, not NNA.

claims.text: On the earnings call published 2025-01-29, Raymond James management said its 'best of both worlds' value proposition combines 'a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture' with the scope of products and capabilities for complex client needs, and that this makes it 'a preferred destination for both current and prospective advisors.'

On the earnings call published 2025-04-23, CEO Paul Shoukry said a change of control at another firm 'always creates a catalyst for advisors to take a look at other options', and that this would 'absolutely increase the opportunities' with advisors seeking the culture and capabilities Raymond James provides. He also said a strong balance sheet 'becomes increasingly important to prospective advisors' seeking strength and stability.

On the earnings call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry contrasted Raymond James with competitors. He said Raymond James attracts advisors 'with our unique culture, leading service, and robust platform, whereas many of our competitors compete with the largest check'. He said many competitors 'are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years'. He also said many competitors 'change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products', whereas Raymond James values independence. He added that a stable platform matters amid industry M&A consolidation and disruption.

On the earnings call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said advisors are 'coming from, you know, wires, regionals, other independents'. He said Raymond James has 'the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody', with critical mass and decades of experience in each. He described the draw as the value proposition, cultural fit, platform and multiple affiliation options.

On the call published 2026-01-28, management said its private wealth advisor program and expanded alternative investments platform support advisors who focus on high-net-worth clients. It also cited the newly launched proprietary digital AI operations agent 'Rai'.

On the earnings call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said 'advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities'. He tied this to the firm's strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and 'commitment to independence', and cited more than $1.1 billion in annual technology spend.

On the earnings call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry cited a '97% adviser satisfaction rate' from the firm's surveys. He said Raymond James has 'all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want' and is 'agnostic' about how an adviser affiliates, wanting advisers to 'fall in love with our culture, values and the platform'.

Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) describes AdvisorChoice® as five options: Traditional Employee (book ownership), Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. The firm's 10-K for the year ended 2025-09-30 also lists RIA and Custody Services as a way advisors affiliate. The Traditional Employee page (as of 2026-05-16) promises 'no quotas, no product pushing' and book ownership.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]; RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF press page content as of 2026-05-16 [IR]

claims.text: Trade press (InvestmentNews, published 2026-11-04; indicative only) reports that an Ohio team joining Raymond James cited culture and leadership stability. It describes 'a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026' as advisors at the wirehouse respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

On the earnings call published 2025-01-29, management said it recruited advisors with approximately $318 million of trailing 12-month production and $51 billion of client assets at their previous firms over the prior 12 months. It said total recruited client assets, including RCS, were nearly $61 billion across all platforms.

On the earnings call published 2025-10-22, management reported fiscal 2025 record recruiting to the domestic independent contractor and employee channels. Trailing 12-month production at previous firms was $407 million, a 21% increase over the prior record. Those advisors had approximately $58 billion of client assets, and total recruited assets including RCS were nearly $63 billion. The firm also reported a record number of financial advisors, 8,943. Shoukry said the pipeline for fiscal 2026 was 'probably the strongest it's ever been entering the fiscal year'.

On the earnings call published 2026-01-28, management reported the first-quarter recruiting result. Trailing 12-month production totaled $96 million and client assets at previous firms were approximately $13 billion. Over the past twelve months, recruited production was nearly $460 million and client assets were over $63 billion. Including RCS, total recruited assets were more than $69 billion. Shoukry said activity was 'broad-based across our affiliation options', 'maybe more heavily tilted in the last six months on the independent contractor side'.

On the earnings call published 2026-04-22 (quarter ended 2026-03-31), management reported recruited production of $141 million and nearly $21 billion of client assets at previous firms. It called this the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history for both recruited production and assets. Management cited 'a robust adviser recruiting pipeline and a strong number of financial advisers who have made commitments to join in the coming quarters'.

On the earnings call published 2026-07-22 (quarter ended 2026-06-30), management reported quarterly recruited production of $156 million and nearly $23 billion of client assets at previous firms. For the first 9 months of the fiscal year, trailing 12-month production totaled $393 million and client assets more than $56 billion. Shoukry said this put the firm 'on a clear path to exceed the record results set in fiscal 2025'. He said the source of recruiting success and the current pipeline 'remains diverse across our affiliation options'.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-10-29; indicative only) reports recruited-advisor trailing 12-month production of $538 million for the fiscal year, up from $407 million, representing more than $82 billion in client assets, per Shoukry on the fiscal fourth-quarter call. It says Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount and had about 8,900 advisors the last time it was broken out.

Trade press (InvestmentNews, published 2026-11-05; indicative only) says Raymond James brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley earlier in 2026 with combined assets exceeding $1 billion. A separate report (published 2026-09-02) describes a UBS team with more than $550 million joining.
claims.source_label: RJF trade 2026-11-05 [trade press (indicative only)]; RJF trade 2026-09-02 [trade press (indicative only)]

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (period ended 2025-09-30) says independent contractor advisors bear their direct costs and 'receive a higher payout percentage' than employee advisors. On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said much more of the last year's recruiting has come from the independent side, and that the employee side has tiered payouts that rise with production.
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists headline terms. Traditional Employee requires a minimum of 5 years of experience and offers up to 50% payout. Advisor Select requires a minimum of 3 years and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue, with 70-80% gross payout. Independent Contractor offers 81% to 90% payout, with a minimum T12 of $150,000 to join an existing branch and $400,000 to open a new branch. Corporate RIA offers 81% to 90% payout.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: On the call published 2025-10-22, the CFO said fiscal 2025 adjusted compensation expense included amortization of transition assistance for recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors totaling $355 million, up approximately 11% from fiscal 2024.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said the firm broke out retention and transition assistance expense for the first time because recruiting is comparable to 'a pretty decent size acquisition'. He said the firm prefers to recruit one by one because '100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller'. On the call published 2026-04-22 he repeated this and said the firm sees 'very good returns' on recruiting.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said 'We have to have a competitive check, but we want the advisors that want to be here over the long term'. He said dialing recruiting spend up or down quarter by quarter yields advisors 'moving or not moving for the highest check'. On the call published 2026-07-22 he said 'we don't lead with the highest check', that 'we have to have competitive economics', and that the firm has 'always been disciplined' on transition assistance.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says other financial services firms are 'offering guaranteed contracts, upfront payments, and increased compensation'. It also says Raymond James's results may be adversely affected by the costs of loans or other incentives it offers to newly recruited advisors.

On the call published 2025-07-23, Shoukry said 'the environment remains competitive' and that PE-backed roll-ups have been 'extremely aggressive' over the last three years, paying higher multiples. He added that 'in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks', and that the firm was still seeing pressure on its existing advisor base.

On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry said 'there are still very rich deals out there from the roll-ups and aggregators'. He said the firm would lose a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets through bank M&A. He said recruiting was 'showing no real signs of slowing down'.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) names an industry-wide trend of advisors departing traditional firms, including for RIAs backed by private equity. It says this 'has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment'. It also says competition for talent is intense and 'could negatively affect earnings'.

On the call published 2026-01-28, Shoukry said 'there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups'. He said the advisors Raymond James recruits are not looking for 'a three-five-year destination' with another liquidity event.

On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said catalysts arise 'every 12 to 18 months'. He said private equity and some strategic firms have been competitive, and that he had heard of 'at least 1 or 2 firms that have tried to raise capital' and were unable to. He reported an uptick in commits in the employee affiliation option.

On the call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry said recruiting 'is not something you could turn on and off quarter-to-quarter' and that the firm wants to 'remain consistent'. He said the firm's growth 'remains focused on quality over quantity'. Raymond James describes no pullback in recruiting in these passages.

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Advisor Services as providing custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors and recordkeepers. It says management has adopted a firm-wide strategy described as "Through Clients' Eyes."

The 2025 10-K states that management believes Schwab can maintain its competitive position in Advisor Services primarily through sales, support, technology and business consulting teams "dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed." The filing also says Schwab uses technology to provide RIAs with a "highly-developed, scalable platform."

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone. He cited lending support, alternatives capability, an institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform with funds from nearly 60 managers, and the Advisor ProDirect launch for breakaway advisors.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Wurster named three Advisor Services monetization areas: wealth (Model Market Center and alternative investments), expanding lending and trust services to advisors through Charles Schwab Bank, and "industry-leading trading capabilities," including a high-touch block-trade service planned for Q1. He also said Schwab is "winning on all fronts in Advisor Services" and that the business grew about 6.5% organically last year.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster said Schwab is continuing to enhance digital experiences across RIA workflows such as move money, account open and account maintenance, while modernizing tools on its adviser platform.

On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Wurster said Schwab has continued to expand its branch footprint and hire financial consultants, wealth advisers and relationship managers for RIA clients while advancing AI capabilities.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said Schwab built its adviser business around "helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed." He described a platform bringing together custody, trading, banking and lending, technology and dedicated service. He said more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian last year, "more than 3x the number of the next closest provider," and that Schwab is continuing to invest in the business. He also said Schwab is the first RIA custodian included in Anthropic's Claude for Financial Advisors.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29; indicative only) reports that Wurster said Schwab wants RIAs to have equal or better access than wirehouse counterparts to lending, private market investing and long-short strategies. It quotes him saying Schwab is "increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank." Separate trade press (2026-10-28) reports he committed to keep serving RIAs with under $100 million in client assets.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-08-26; indicative only) reports that Vanguard's $4.6 billion outlay for Altruist makes it a more formidable RIA-custody competitor. It quotes Datos Insights' Will Trout saying that "Both have absorbed real share loss to Altruist already," and that Schwab and Fidelity still have a commanding lead. This is an analyst view, not a Schwab statement.

Pulling back on referrals: trade press (InvestmentNews, 2026-08-24; indicative only) reports that a Schwab spokesperson confirmed the Schwab Advisor Network referral minimum rises from $2 million to $5 million effective Jan. 5, 2027. It follows an earlier rise from $500,000 to $2 million. Trade press (2026-10-15) adds that the AUM threshold for firms entering SAN rose to at least $500 million from $250 million. The 2026-10-28 article quotes Wurster saying SAN has 100 participating firms out of the 17,000 custodying with Schwab and that Schwab will continue to invest in SAN. On the 3Q26 call, Wurster said more than 16,000 firms represent $5.8 trillion, and more than 1,100 firms added Schwab as custodian last year. claims.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-15; indicative only) reports that Schwab said it added 1,001 new RIAs to its custody platform in Q3, versus 349, 339, 202 and 79 for its nearest unnamed peers. Trade press (RIABiz, 2026-09-23; indicative only) reports specific breakaway wins custodying at Schwab, including Rise Private Wealth Management, which it says is near $8 billion in assets, and StackStone Wealth at $1.9 billion in assets administered.

The 2025 10-K describes the RIA technology platform: the Advisor Services website for account opening, money movement, transfers and trading; third-party integrations; Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect, available free of charge to advisors; the thinkpipes trading platform; and iRebal for rebalancing. It also describes consulting services, transition support and the Advisor ProDirect membership program launched in 2025.

Pricing and economics: the 2025 10-K says that as custodian, Schwab earns revenue on the underlying client assets, predominantly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. It states that Schwab does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee. The 10-K also says net revenues in both segments come from client assets and trading activity, with differences based on asset composition, trading frequency and pricing unique to each segment.

Banking and lending: on the 2Q26 call (July 2026), Wurster said RIAs value the bank because they do not have to introduce another relationship to their clients. He said lending balances rose 33% year over year, driven in large part by the digital Pledged Asset Line, and that Schwab is adding structured asset lending. Schwab took a minority stake in Nevis, a back-office AI platform, which is to go live for advisors in Q1 2027 and which RIAs pay for separately. The Wealth.com tax and estate tool is free until February 2027 and fee-based afterwards. Schwab now requires Docusign for agreements. Syntax Direct integrates with iRebal. Beatty said a business banking checking account is coming next year.

claims.text: On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-14), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, and that results "reflect strong demand for advice, and our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform."

On the 2Q26 earnings call (published 2026-07-14), Borthwick said the Merrill leaders are trying to "just keep growing the sales force," that the aim is 5% "over the course of the next 3 to 5 years" (the "Merrill 5% guide"), and that "adviser attrition is now at near historic lows."

On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-14), Borthwick said both Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform and our ability to deliver comprehensive solutions for clients."

On the 1Q26 call (published 2026-04-15), Borthwick said the firm is "driving productivity higher on both newer and existing members of our financial advisers team, and we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers."

On the 4Q25 call (published 2026-01-14), Borthwick said "we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy," and pointed to a training program for wealth management, Bank of America and Merrill as what the firm can "keep driving" to improve net new flows.

Merrill's Advisor Development Program recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes training as the entry route: it offers "industry leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses," base salary and "unlimited earning potential," and coaching and mentorship. It lists the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 licences, an approximately 13-month path that includes three months of licensing, and a Financial Advisor stage of approximately 1-4 years before progression to Merrill Core Advisor.

claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm has been investing over multiple years in its processes and systems to have robust infrastructure for growth, including technology, a better understanding of its data, and better servicing of clients, in the context of the Wealth Management platform.

On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said the firm is investing in E*TRADE, and that financial advisors see the integrated firm as offering "unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating." The CFO said the firm has been investing in its self-directed platform, including marketing, and cited benefits from platform investments made over multiple years.

On the 2Q25 earnings call (July 2025), Pick described "ongoing investments in our world-class platform, including investments to support our advisors, a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel" as an engine for future growth.

On the 3Q25 earnings call (October 2025), the CFO said early AI use cases, some live and some in pilot, are showing progress. She named DevGen AI (developer efficiency by modernizing code), Parable (an interactive data analysis and summarization tool), and LeadIQ, an AI-powered lead distribution platform that matches workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitates engagement with financial advisors. Pick said the mantra is to scale with key clients, build out product capabilities and invest in technologies, some efficiency-driven and some effectiveness-driven.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Pick said the firm continues to invest in Wealth, Institutional Securities and Investment Management "via human capital and technology," and that its growth plans embed increasing adoption of AI tools throughout the enterprise. He said the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

On the same 4Q25 call (January 2026), a company representative said LeadIQ is helping introduce advisors to clients interested in advice using AI, and that technology on the revenue and expense sides should help drive margin.

The 2025 10-K (published February 2026) states that the Wealth Management segment's ability to compete across advisor-led, workplace and digital direct channels is affected by multiple factors, including "our technology supporting evolving client needs, including generative artificial intelligence and tokenization."

On the 1Q26 earnings call (April 2026), Pick said the firm's strategy is, in part, "to invest in our clients and technology across the integrated firm." He called AI platforms additive to what the firm has: world-class technology, world-class cyber defense, and trusted advisers sitting with the client, which he called the key.

On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), Pick said the firm has built advantages around its self-directed channel, workplace offering and adviser-client relationships that "make technology a differentiator in our favor."

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says the firm offers multiple affiliation options, which it calls AdvisorChoice®. Advisors primarily affiliate directly as employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division. It describes employee advisors as working in a traditional branch with local management and administrative staff, serving predominantly retail clients, and paid primarily through a payout on revenues they generate.

Raymond James's affiliation-options recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists five AdvisorChoice® options: Traditional Employee ("book ownership"), Advisor Select ("Lead your own branch with access to administrative support and full corporate benefits"), Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA ("true autonomy" for fee-only practices). A separate RIA & Custody Services option is also listed.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The same page (as of 2026-04-21) gives headline terms. Traditional Employee: minimum 5 years of experience, up to 50% payout and a full employee benefits offering. Advisor Select: 70-80% gross payout, with a minimum of $3.5 million in annual branch fees and commission revenue. Independent Contractor: 81% to 90% payout, with a third-party benefits package. Corporate RIA: 81% to 90% payout, with minimum $50 million in assets under advisement. Bank & Credit Union: compensation is set by the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James. RIA & Custody Services: compensation is determined by the RIA or broker/dealer, who is also responsible for compliance.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Raymond James's own recruiting pages (content as of dates in 2026) pitch each model separately. Advisor Select (as of 2026-03-11) is "an employee affiliation option" for entrepreneurial advisors who run their branch's P&L "to earn a higher rate on production". The Independent Advisor page (as of 2026-05-19) offers "a partnership in independence" backed by a self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer. The Corporate RIA is described as an "all-inclusive" model that streamlines the burdens of an RIA. The RCS page (as of 2026-07-12) promises "complete freedom and control", "free from retail conflict", with the user choosing "as much – or as little" of the firm's support as needed.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-03-11 [IR]; RJF press page content as of 2026-05-19 [IR]; RJF press page content as of 2026-07-12 [IR]

claims.text: On earnings calls, management frames the value proposition as one "best of both worlds" offer across all options. On the 2Q FY25 call (April 2025) and the 3Q FY25 call (October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry described a combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology and solutions that "continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options". On the 4Q FY25 call (January 2026) he said the firm has "the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody", with "critical mass and decades of experience in all of them". On the call published 2026-07-22 he said the firm is "agnostic" on how an advisor affiliates and "indifferent" to it.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-03-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: On the call published 2026-07-22, Shoukry said advisors differ in how they spend their time across the options. Some want to spend close to 100% of their time on books of business and clients, which he said is "more aligned with the employee affiliation option". Others also want to run a business: building a team, paying for benefits, real estate and legal matters.

The 2025 10-K (as of September 30) shows financial advisors by channel. Employees: 3,878 (2025), 3,826 (2024), 3,693 (2023). Independent contractors: 5,065 (2025), 4,961 (2024), 5,019 (2023). Total: 8,943, 8,787 and 8,712. RCS advisors are not included in this advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.

On the 3Q FY24 call (October 2024), then-CEO Paul Reilly said RCS had "by far the highest percentage growth". In total dollars the lead alternates: "a couple of years ago, it was independent. This year, the employee channel really led the way." He said the old pattern that independents grow faster in up markets is no longer seen: "It is really just where we can meet the teams that like an affiliation option." RCS client assets were $181 billion, up 36% over the prior year.

On the 4Q FY24 call (January 2025), RCS finished the quarter with $188 billion of client assets under administration, up 28% year-over-year. The investor-day deck (published 2025-06-05), in a slide titled "Strong asset growth across our multiple affiliation models", charts domestic PCG AUA for Employee, Independent contractor and RCS between Mar. 31, 2020 and Mar. 31, 2025. It labels 5-year CAGRs of 32%, 11%, 14% and 14%. The extracted text does not tie each figure to a channel.

On the 2Q FY25 call (July 2025), Shoukry said the firm sees "good success across all of our affiliation options". He said "the acceleration rate within the independent channel is probably higher", with very good success in the employee and independent RIA options as well.

The 10-Q filings show PCG AUA from firms affiliated through RCS. On Dec 31, 2025 it was $224.6 billion, versus $217.3 billion on Sep 30, 2025 and $188.2 billion on Dec 31, 2024. On Jun 30, 2026 it was $251.3 billion, versus $228.2 billion on Mar 31, 2026 and $201.6 billion on Jun 30, 2025. The firm says RCS growth is "partially due to transfers into RCS from our other financial advisor channels", but it does not expect such transfers to significantly impact results of operations.

On the call published 2026-04-22, Shoukry said "we're actually seeing pretty good uptick in the employee affiliation option as well". He said the "mix shift" he had referred to concerned the compensation ratio, because of "the payout difference in the independent channel versus the employee channel". He added that independent-side catalysts should not "overshadow" employee-side success, which "continues to tick up".

The firm has recruited across channels, with each period's figures stated on its call. Recruited advisors' trailing 12-month production at previous firms (domestic independent contractor and employee channels) and client assets:
- FY24 (call published 2024-10-23): approximately $335 million and $56.7 billion.
- FY25 (call published 2025-10-22): $407 million, up 21%, and approximately $58 billion; nearly $63 billion in total client assets across all platforms including RAA and Custody Services.
- Past 12 months to the call published 2026-01-28: nearly $460 million and over $63 billion; more than $69 billion across all platforms.
- Quarter reported 2026-04-22: $141 million and nearly $21 billion.
- Quarter reported 2026-07-22: $156 million and nearly $23 billion; $393 million and more than $56 billion for the first 9 months of the fiscal year.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2024-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Management describes recruiting as broad-based across models. On the call published 2025-10-22, Shoukry said recruiting has been "broad-based across all of our affiliation options, the employee, independent contractor, and the RAA custody channels". On the call published 2026-07-22 he said the source of recruiting success and the pipeline "remains diverse across our affiliation options". On the call published 2025-07-23 he said M&A-driven catalysts, "particularly on the independent side", contributed to the acceleration in the pipeline but success was not concentrated there. On the call published 2026-04-22 he cited an "uptick of commits" in the employee option.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-06-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-06-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]

claims.text: On moves out of a model, Reilly said on the 3Q FY24 call (October 2024) that a couple of OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division were leaving. Roughly $3 billion of AUA left in the fiscal fourth quarter, with approximately $5 billion more expected early in fiscal 2025. On the call published 2025-01-29 he cited the departure of primarily one large branch in the independent contractor division, with an impact of approximately $5 billion of AUA.

The 2025 10-K names the risk of advisors departing traditional firms, including "to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs", some PE-backed. It says that if departures continue or accelerate, including transition "to an unaffiliated RIA channel", this could adversely affect PCG results. The firm says it seeks to mitigate this through succession planning and a broad range of services.

Management's stated priorities on recruiting and retention, with the date of each call:
- Call published 2026-04-22: Shoukry said the firm prefers to "recruit 1 by 1" rather than acquire, because "100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser". He said it has ramped up recruiting substantially year over year and broken out recruiting and retention costs.
- Call published 2026-07-22: he said recruiting "is not something you could turn on and off quarter-to-quarter" and that consistency across affiliation options is critical.
- Call published 2026-04-22: he said continued investment in automation, process improvement and AI is part of "more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend".

On competition, Shoukry said on the call published 2025-07-23 that PE-backed roll-ups have been "extremely aggressive" in paying higher multiples. He said "we are still seeing pressure on the existing advisor base, private equity", and that roll-ups "compete with big checks" in the absence of a value proposition. On the call published 2026-01-28 he said competition has increased, but the firm feels it has "in some ways, less competition than ever". He cited its long-term focus, its commitment to remaining independent and its technology investment of about $1 billion, which he said many similar-culture competitors do not match. On the call published 2026-04-22 he said private equity "has certainly been competitive over the last 5 years".
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-06-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]

claims.text: The 2025 10-K names competitive risks. It describes "a highly competitive recruiting environment" tied to the industry-wide departure of advisors to independent RIAs. It also notes claims of unfair hiring practices, and that participation in the voluntary Protocol for Broker Recruiting could change if competitors withdraw.

Where management acknowledges ground lost: the independent contractor division lost OSJ relationships and a large branch in fiscal 2024-25, with roughly $3 billion, $5 billion and approximately $5 billion of AUA cited across the calls. Management also pointed to a compensation-ratio effect from a shift toward the independent channel, because of the payout difference versus the employee channel.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2024-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2024-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said advisors see "compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating" and that the firm is "selective" while getting a lot of inbound inquiry.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 3Q25 10-Q (November 2025) attributes higher compensation expense to "an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors on higher revenues" and higher expenses related to outstanding deferred compensation.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (August 2026) states that deferred compensation for Wealth Management financial advisors is generally 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards, and that the programs generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: On the 1Q25 and 2Q25 Bank of America calls (April and July 2025), the CFO cited the cost of hiring to add experienced advisors to the platform in Merrill and the Private Bank as part of GWIM expense growth.
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2025-03-31 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2025-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "Base salary and unlimited earning potential" and "High-quality leads and direct client interactions" among what it offers. It states no payout percentages.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Merrill: Merrill's advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes infrastructure that supports lead generation through Bank of America's global bank, trust division and market presence, plus access to Merrill's wealth management platform.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: Raymond James's affiliation options page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists headline payouts by model: Traditional Employee up to 50%; Advisor Select 70-80% gross payout; Independent Contractor 81% to 90%; Corporate RIA 81% to 90%. Bank & Credit Union advisors receive a compensation package from the financial institution in partnership with Raymond James.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm broke out retention and transition assistance expense for the first time. He said the firm prefers to recruit advisors one by one because "100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller." On the 1Q26 call (April 2026) he repeated the point and said annual recruiting is now comparable to a medium-sized acquisition.

Compensation and recruiting incentives - Raymond James: The 2Q26 supplement (July 2026) says PCG recruiting and retention-related compensation covers cash and equity awards issued for recruiting, as retention for existing advisors, or with acquisitions. These awards are expensed over the requisite service period, "typically between 5 and 10 years".

Training and development - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) describes firm-wide talent development programs and says management believes "supporting employee development and growth contributes to long-term retention." This is not specific to financial advisors.

Training and development - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), Ted Pick said the firm is investing in broadening capabilities for FAs, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

Training and development - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program page (page content as of 2026-11-03) lists "Industry leading training and dedicated study time to obtain securities licenses". Path A (ADP Client Associate) and Path B (ADP Financial Solutions Advisor) each run approximately 13 months and involve the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66. The ADP Financial Advisor stage runs approximately 1-4 years before progression to Merrill Core Advisor.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Training and development - Merrill: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the Bank of America CFO said recruiting experienced advisors "isn't an enormous part of our strategy" but that the firm has a training program to train people in wealth management, Bank of America and Merrill. He said this is what the firm believes it can keep driving to improve net new flows.

Training and development - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (November 2025) says aspiring advisors can gain branch experience through the Wealth Management Associate Program or move to the Advisor Mastery Program to begin building a client base. It also describes a department providing business coaching and national conferences for the employee and independent contractor channels.

Training and development - Raymond James: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), Paul Shoukry said that in private wealth the firm is focused on education, training, accreditation and enhanced capabilities for advisors serving sophisticated clients.

Results - Morgan Stanley: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), management cited 2025 Wealth Management net new assets of $356 billion and fee-based flows of $160 billion. Ted Pick said $100 billion migrated to financial advisors in 2025. These are asset-flow results, not advisor recruiting or retention counts.

Results - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) reports firm-wide voluntary attrition in 2025 of 9% (global, all employees). On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), Ted Pick said the firm retains 99% of its clients. Neither is an advisor attrition figure.

Results - Merrill: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), the Bank of America CFO said Merrill and the Private Bank continued to add financial advisors through the extensive training program and experienced hiring. She said approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

Results - Merrill: On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), CFO Alastair Borthwick said of the Merrill 5% guide (over the next 3 to 5 years) that the firm is "off to a good start". He said the aim is to keep growing the sales force and that "adviser attrition is now at near historic lows." No attrition figure was given.

Results - Merrill: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said the results reflect "our ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform."

Results - Raymond James: On the 4Q25 call (October 2025), management said it ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, reflecting solid retention and strong recruiting. The FY2025 10-K counts 8,943 employee and independent contractor advisors as of September 30, 2025. FY2025 recruits had trailing 12-month production of $407 million (a 21% increase over the prior record) and approximately $58 billion of client assets at their previous firms.

Results - Raymond James: On the 1Q26 call (January 2026), management said trailing 12-month recruited production was nearly $460 million and client assets were over $63 billion. On the 2Q26 call (April 2026), the quarter's recruits had $141 million of production and nearly $21 billion of assets. On the 3Q26 call (July 2026), the quarter's recruits had $156 million and nearly $23 billion. In July 2026, Shoukry cited a 97% adviser satisfaction rate in firm surveys.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Competitive positioning - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) says the firm competes for clients, market share and human talent, and that competition is intense. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said the firm has $8.4 trillion in client assets and nearly 21 million relationships. He called its platform and scale a "powerful competitive advantage".

Competitive positioning - Merrill: On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), the Bank of America CFO said "the Merrill FA see the value of our franchise." On the 2Q26 call (July 2026), he said Merrill and the Private Bank "continued to attract talented advisers who are drawn to the breadth of our platform."
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2025-12-31 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Competitive positioning - Raymond James: On the 4Q25 call (October 2025), Paul Shoukry contrasted the firm with competitors. He said many compete "with the largest check", change comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products, and look for an exit in three to five years. In January 2026 he said advisors are coming from wirehouses, regionals and other independents, and that the firm has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options. In April 2026 he called private equity competitive over the last 5 years.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2025-09-30 [IR]; RJF transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]; RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]

claims.text: Pullback or losses - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (February 2026) lists as a risk that compensation costs to attract and retain employees may increase, and that more stringent regulation of employee compensation "could have an adverse effect on our ability to hire or retain the most qualified employees." This is a firm-wide risk statement, not an advisor loss figure.

Pullback or losses - Raymond James: On the 4Q24 call (October 2024), management said a few OSJ relationships in the independent contractor division were leaving, with roughly $3 billion of AUA leaving in the fiscal fourth quarter and about $5 billion more expected to transfer in early fiscal 2025. On the 4Q25 call (October 2025), Paul Shoukry said a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets would be lost through bank M&A.

Pullback or losses - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (November 2025) names risks from the industry-wide trend of advisors departing traditional firms, including to private-equity-backed RIAs. It says AUA "has been and may continue to be negatively impacted" if it fails to retain or recruit advisors. It also notes that other firms offer guaranteed contracts and upfront payments.

claims.text: Value proposition - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says Schwab's Advisor Services segment has become one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs. Management believes it keeps its competitive position mainly through sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams "dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed." It says it pairs superior service with technology that gives RIAs a "highly-developed, scalable platform" for administering client assets.

Value proposition - Schwab: The 2025 10-K describes proprietary advisor software and the Advisor Services website as the core platform for account opening, money movement, transfers, trading and service. It lists integrations with third-party CRM, portfolio-management, trade-order and planning tools. It also lists Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect (free to advisors), thinkpipes and iRebal.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building "a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone." He cited more lending support, alternatives capability, an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform with funds from nearly 60 managers, and the launch of Advisor ProDirect for breakaway advisors.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster called Schwab the "leading custodial offer" and said its "value proposition to advisers has never been stronger." He cited added lending, including a structured asset lending program that lets advisors keep clients' borrowing against alternatives and restricted or private shares in-house. He also said Schwab is enhancing digital RIA workflows (move money, account open, account maintenance) and modernizing advisor-platform tools.

Value proposition - Schwab: The May 2026 investor day deck describes "the leading RIA support ecosystem," providing wealth tools, investment/lending products and technology "in addition to custody & service." It also says Schwab will expand value-added RIA offerings and modernize platforms.

Value proposition - Schwab: On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said the advisor business serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets, on a platform combining custody, trading, banking and lending, technology, and dedicated service and support. He said the business requires scale, trust and operational excellence, and that more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as custodian last year, "more than 3x the number of the next closest provider." The October 2026 press release highlights a partnership with Anthropic to bring Claude for Financial Advisors to the independent RIAs Schwab serves.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the FY2025 3Q-era calls (the 2Q25 call was published July 2025 and the 3Q25 call October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry described a "best of both worlds" value proposition. It combines an "advisor and client-focused culture" with "leading technology and solutions," and he said it resonates across all affiliation options. He added that the firm's strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are a differentiator, and that a stable platform matters amid short-term and leveraged-backed players and industry M&A.

Value proposition - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) says the firm's ability to attract advisors rests on its "values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors." It cites business coaching and growth tools, and separate national conferences for the employee and independent contractor channels. It describes AdvisorChoice, under which advisors affiliate as employees, as independent contractors, or through the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the 1Q FY26 call (published January 2026), Shoukry cited the "largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody," with "critical mass and decades of experience in all of them." He tied this to cultural fit and platform. He also cited the private wealth advisor program, an expanded alternatives platform, and a newly launched proprietary AI operations agent named Rai.

Value proposition - Raymond James: On the call published April 2026, Shoukry said "advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities." He credited a client-focused culture, leading technologies and products, a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence. He said the firm will keep investing in automation, process improvement and AI as part of a "more than $1.1 billion annual technology spend." On the call published July 2026 he repeated this and cited "near record levels of adviser satisfaction" and investment in private wealth tools.

Value proposition - Raymond James: Its independent-advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-05-19) pitches "A partnership in independence." It says independent contractors can "access our full capabilities at a level that's right for your business" with a full-service, self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer. It lists private wealth concierge support, advisor-built technology, marketing, business consulting, succession and acquisition guidance, paraplanning, admin extension, and a Corporate RIA model.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-05-19 [IR]

claims.text: Value proposition - Raymond James: The RIA & Custody Services page (page content as of 2026-07-12) says RCS gives RIAs "true strategic, financial and administrative control," "free from retail conflict," using as much or as little of Raymond James's support as needed. It lists a dedicated service associate, transitions management, technology that incorporates third-party applications, marketing, practice management, succession planning and acquisition, and Wealth Strategies for high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-07-12 [IR]

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-28) reports that Wurster told Schwab Impact attendees Schwab will keep focusing on custody for RIAs with under $100 million AUM, saying Schwab's role is "to provide a platform and a support ecosystem that helps you support your clients and helps your firm thrive." It was reported in the context of Fidelity's move to push out such firms.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29) reports Shoukry saying Raymond James has the largest total addressable market because all affiliation options are offered at scale, so advisors can focus on cultural fit and capabilities. The independent contractor channel draws the most dollar interest, and RIA custody is growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

claims.text: Asset thresholds - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) describes Wealth Management clients only in general terms, as individual investors "including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions." No numeric asset or investable-asset tiers appear in the evidence.

Asset thresholds - Merrill: The BAC 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business is staffed by financial advisors "focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets." It says Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, targets high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. The 10-K gives no dollar figure for that upper tier.

Asset thresholds - Merrill: In footnotes to the 1Q26 deck (published 2026-04-15), the 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-14) and the 3Q26 press release (published 2026-10-14), Bank of America defines Merrill primary households as "$250K+ in investable assets." It defines Private Bank core relationships as "$3MM+ in total balances."
claims.source_label: BAC deck - GWIM segment 2026-03-31, p.14 [IR]; BAC deck - GWIM segment 2026-06-30, p.14 [IR]; BAC press - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [filing]

claims.text: Asset thresholds - Merrill: On the 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets. He said the Private Bank added 470 net new relationships with at least $3 million under management. The 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-14) reports about 5.4K net new $500K+ households in Merrill and about 430 net new $3MM+ relationships in the Private Bank.
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [IR]; BAC deck - GWIM segment 2026-06-30, p.14 [IR]

claims.text: Channels - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that Wealth Management "supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace." The 2Q26 supplement (published 2026-07-15) reports advisor-led client assets of $6,273 billion and self-directed client assets of $1,811 billion at June 30, 2026. It also reports stock plan unvested public assets of $658 billion for the workplace channel. Channel is the organizing line in the evidence, not wealth tier.
claims.source_label: MS 10-K 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS supplement - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30, p.8 [IR]

claims.text: Channels - Merrill: The BAC 10-Q for 2Q26 (published 2026-07-31) says GWIM "consists of two primary businesses: Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank." The 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-10-14) shows client balances at period end of $4,240,601 million for Merrill Wealth Management and $816,186 million for Bank of America Private Bank. The 2025 10-K places Private Wealth Management inside Merrill Wealth Management and pairs it with the Private Bank for high net worth and ultra high net worth clients.
claims.source_label: BAC 10-Q - GWIM segment 2026-06-30 [filing]; BAC supplement - GWIM segment 2026-09-30, p.18 [IR]; BAC 10-K - GWIM segment 2025-12-31 [filing]

claims.text: Service model - Morgan Stanley: Per the 4Q25 supplement (published 2026-01-15), advisor-led client assets are "client assets in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned." Self-directed client assets are "active accounts which are not advisor-led," and active means at least $25 in assets. The workplace channel "includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees." On the 1Q25 call (April 2025) the CFO said about $300 billion had migrated into advisor-led accounts from workplace since the channel was expanded in 2020. Management describes this as a funnel of relationships feeding the advisor-led channel.
claims.source_label: MS supplement 2025-12-31, p.15 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-03-31 [IR]; MS transcript 2025-12-31 [IR]

claims.text: Service model - Merrill: The BAC 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business as "a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors," offering investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products. It describes the Private Bank and Private Wealth Management offering as comprehensive wealth management solutions with customized wealth structuring, investment management, trust and banking services, including specialty asset management. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CFO said 67% of Merrill clients have banking relationships with Bank of America.

claims.text: Explicit statements - Merrill: Merrill (inside Bank of America's GWIM) is the only one of the five whose own materials use the term. A Bank of America GWIM investor-day slide (published 2025-11-05) lays out a "Wealth Continuum" that labels "Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)" and "High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)". The slide is a GWIM slide (Merrill plus the Private Bank) and does not itself name Merrill.

Explicit statements - Merrill: The Bank of America 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13 per the filing set; GWIM section) states that Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides "a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets." It does not use the words "mass affluent".

Explicit statements - Schwab: Schwab speaks of "affluent" clients and does not use "mass affluent" in the evidence. On the 4Q25 earnings call (published 2026-01-21) CEO Rick Wurster said "About one-third of new clients are affluent" and that Schwab is "winning with investors of all ages, wealth tiers, and time horizons."

Explicit statements - Schwab: On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-21), Wurster said 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate wealth and banking relationships, and that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm "jumped 11 percentage points year-over-year to 22%".

Definition and thresholds - Merrill: In the Bank of America GWIM investor-day deck (2025-11-05), the "Mass Affluent" tier is defined as $500K - $1MM, and the next tier, High Net Worth, as $1MM - $10MM. Separately, the 2025 10-K says Merrill's advisory business focuses on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets, and a 1Q26 GWIM deck (published 2026-04-15) describes Merrill primary households as those with $250K+ in investable assets. The evidence does not reconcile the $250K and $500K lines.
claims.source_label: BAC deck - GWIM segment 2025-11-05, p.7 [IR]; BAC 10-K - GWIM segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; BAC deck - GWIM segment 2026-03-31, p.14 [IR]

claims.text: Strategy and products - Schwab: At its May 2026 investor day (deck published 2026-05-14), Schwab presented a slide on growing advice share and cited "68% of affluent investors want & are willing to pay for advice". On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-21), Wurster said more retail clients seek "holistic financial advice delivered seamlessly on their terms through a combination of people and increasingly AI-enabled technology". He said Schwab is investing heavily in Schwab Wealth Advisory, including tax, trust and estate capabilities, and that its Client Promoter Score is the highest of any Schwab offer. These statements refer to affluent investors and retail clients, not to a defined mass-affluent segment.

Strategy and products - Merrill: The Bank of America 2025 10-K says Merrill Wealth Management provides "tailored solutions" through "a full set of investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products" to clients with over $250,000 in investable assets. In the GWIM investor-day deck (2025-11-05), management said it believes "the Wealth Continuum allows us to deliver as one company" and that it has "the capabilities to deliver for every client in the way they want to be served". On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), the CFO cited advisor productivity, digital engagement and AI tools that "expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale", and said 67% of Merrill clients have banking relationships with the firm.
claims.source_label: BAC 10-K - GWIM segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; BAC deck - GWIM segment 2025-11-05, p.3 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [IR]

claims.text: Growth priorities and results - Schwab: On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-21), Wurster said about one-third of new clients are affluent. On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-21), he said that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one firm rose to 22% and "we expect this to grow as more investors seek the convenience of one-stop shopping." Schwab does not report separate results for a mass-affluent segment in the evidence.

Growth priorities and results - Merrill: GWIM's 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-14) reports about 5.4K net new $500K+ households added in Merrill in 2Q26. On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%, and attributed this to "strong demand for advice". The $500K+ measure spans the deck's mass-affluent ($500K-$1MM) and higher tiers and is not split by tier.
claims.source_label: BAC deck - GWIM segment 2026-06-30, p.14 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [IR]; BAC deck - GWIM segment 2025-11-05, p.7 [IR]

claims.text: Definition - Morgan Stanley: Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management supplement for the quarter ended December 31, 2020 (published 2021-01-20) labels its advisor headcount line "Wealth Management representatives", shown inside the advisor-led channel, at 15,950. The chunk gives no definition of who counts as a representative, and no more recent supplement in the evidence shows this line.

Definition - Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended 2025-09-26 (published 2025-11-07) reports "Financial advisors (actual)". It defines Attrition % as "the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end." That defines attrition against the period-end count. It does not define who qualifies as a financial advisor.

Definition - Merrill: Merrill's advisor recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes "Merrill Core Advisor (FA)" as the role reached "upon progression", once the Advisor Development Program is completed. Earlier roles are ADP Client Associate, ADP Financial Solutions Advisor and ADP Financial Advisor. This is a role description on a recruiting page, not a headcount definition from a financial filing.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]

claims.text: Definition - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (period 2025-09-30, published 2025-11-25) states the firm "had 8,943 employee and independent contractor financial advisors affiliated with us as of September 30, 2025." It also states that "Advisors in our RCS division are not included in our financial advisor metric although their client assets are included in PCG AUA."

Includes - Schwab: Schwab's investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) describes Schwab Advisor Network advisors as "independent and ... not employees or agents of Charles Schwab & Co., Inc." It says Schwab prescreens them and that they pay referral fees. The chunk does not say whether these advisors, or independent RIAs generally, are counted in any Schwab advisor total.

Includes - Edward Jones: The FY2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) reports financial advisors "(actual)" at year end. The count was 20,425 at year-end 2025, 20,125 at year-end 2024 and 19,232 at year-end 2023. The 10-K notes that "many of the Partnership's financial advisors are employees". The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) says the firm operates in the U.S. and Canada, with "more than 20,000 financial advisors". The evidence does not say whether Associate Financial Advisors or trainees are counted.

Includes - Merrill: Merrill's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-11-03) describes a trainee path to Financial Advisor. It includes Advisor Development Program roles (ADP Client Associate, ADP Financial Solutions Advisor and ADP Financial Advisor, the last described as taking "Approximately 1-4 years") before Merrill Core Advisor. On the 2Q25 call (published 2025-07-16) the Bank of America CFO said the firm "continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors." Neither source says whether trainees are in a reported advisor count.
claims.source_label: MER press page content as of 2026-11-03 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2025-06-30 [IR]

claims.text: Includes - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) breaks the 8,943 total advisors at 2025-09-30 into 3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors. Raymond James says independent contractor advisors may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in its Financial Institutions Division. Management attributed the year's increase to "new recruits and trainees that were moved into production roles" exceeding departures and planned retirements.
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]

claims.text: Excludes - Edward Jones: The 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-26 (published 2026-08-07) reports financial advisors (20,514 at period end) on a separate line from client support team professionals (20,654) and home office associates (8,808). The two support lines carry the footnote "Counted on a full-time equivalent basis". The financial advisor line is labelled "(actual)". The evidence does not say how part-time or retired advisors are treated.

Excludes - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states that advisors in the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division "are not included in our financial advisor metric", although their client assets are in PCG AUA. Separately, the 10-K cites "approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors". It describes associates as including "our employee financial advisors and all of our other employees", so non-advisor employees sit outside the 8,943 advisor metric.
claims.source_label: RJF 10-K 2025-09-30 [filing]; RJF 10-K - Private Client Group segment 2025-09-30 [filing]

claims.text: Reporting - Morgan Stanley: The quarterly Wealth Management supplement for the quarter ended 2020-12-31 (published 2021-01-20) reports "Wealth Management representatives" at period end: 15,950 at Dec 31, 2020, 15,469 at Sep 30, 2020 and 15,468 at Dec 31, 2019. It shows them in the advisor-led channel, with percentage change columns.

Reporting - Schwab: On the 3Q26 earnings call (published 2026-10-15), the CEO described the advisor business by firms rather than advisors: "we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets". Earlier calls and filings mention hiring "financial consultants and wealth advisers" and headcount growth that includes them (2Q26 10-Q, published 2026-08-07). The evidence shows no reported count of those advisors.

Reporting - Edward Jones: The FY2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) reports financial advisors at year end and on average: year-end 20,425 (2025), 20,125 (2024) and 19,232 (2023); average 20,331, 19,650 and 18,945. The 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-26 (published 2026-08-07) reports period-end 20,514 and average 20,537, and in the MD&A tables gives two column sets, one of which reads 19,647 at period end. The 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) states "Financial advisor attrition was 6.1%", with a rise in departures among advisors with tenure of five years or less.

Reporting - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) has a table of financial advisors as of September 30 by channel. 2025: employees 3,878, independent contractors 5,065, total 8,943. 2024: 3,826, 4,961 and 8,787. 2023: 3,693, 5,019 and 8,712. On the 4Q25 call (published 2025-10-22), the CEO cited "a record number of financial advisors of 8,943". Recruiting is reported through trailing-12-month production and client assets at previous firms. On the 3Q FY26 call (published 2026-07-22), the CEO cited $156 million of production and nearly $23 billion of client assets for the quarter's recruits into the domestic independent contractor and employee channels. Management cites "departures and planned retirements" but gives no attrition rate in the evidence. Raymond James's Bank and Credit Union Advisors page (page content as of 2026-05-17) cites 940 advisors across 160 financial institutions.
