claims.text: UBS's next-generation study (published 2026-04-22) reports that experience and expertise top the next generation's wish list when choosing a wealth manager (79%). More than half (56%) want advisors who can build trusted relationships across generations, and 41% want an advisor who fully understands the next generation's needs. The study also reports a gender split: women emphasize experience (90%), frequent engagement (35%) and early commitment to the next generation (40%), while men more often prioritize a deep understanding of their financial goals (49%).

UBS (published 2026-04-22) also reports that two-thirds (67%) of the next generation say a strong personal connection with their advisor is important. Women place greater weight on personal fit and regular contact, while men focus on competitive pricing and specialist expertise.

Cerulli (published 2025-10-29) says younger investors are typically more comfortable directing their own investing through online brokerages. It concludes that advisors trying to reach these prospects must be able to articulate benefits outside investing, such as financial planning, lending and tax services.

Fidelity's 2025 Investor Insights Study (published 2025-10-09) covers wealthy Gen X, Y and Z households. It says they value advisors but seek transparency in advisor compensation, broader life guidance beyond investment management, and emerging investment products such as active ETFs, liquid alternatives and cryptocurrencies. It describes them as focused on holistic financial planning and life goal achievement.

Schwab's Q3 2025 call (published 2025-10-16) says Gen Z investors are turning to Schwab partly because Schwab is meeting them in the channels where they turn for information about investing. Management said it knows they learn about finances primarily through social media and family, and that their top online resource is YouTube. Management calls Schwab the number one financial services firm on YouTube by followers. This is management's own account of why younger clients choose Schwab.

The GSAM alternatives survey (published 2025-10-17) reports that financial media is the most common information source for individual investors, followed by advisors, and that Millennials cite social media more often while Boomers rely on traditional outlets. This is about information sources on alternatives, not advisor search.

The CFPB-cited misinformation survey (published 2025-06-06) found that Americans aged 25-45 are more trusting than those aged 46-64 of financial information from generative AI tools (44% vs. 26%) and social media (44% vs. 24%). Overall, people are most confident in information from a qualified advisor such as a CFP® professional.

UBS (published 2026-04-22) reports that younger adults (22 to 25 years) rely most on peers (57%) as a source of advice in succession planning. On the family's banker, 41% prefer to work with their family's existing bank.

Cerulli (published 2025-10-29) finds just 41% of HNW practices say their clients' children are either established clients or actively involved in the planning process. HNW executives say advisors' relationships with clients' children have been slipping slightly since 2020.

Morgan Stanley's CFO said on the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-15) that for clients who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, the firm is working on a referral model. She said it can begin as early as financial education and with 401(k) assets coming in through workplace. This is a firm statement of approach, not evidence on how younger clients choose.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) lists, among its initiatives, a new digital platform focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors. It says the Partnership cannot reliably predict the timing or outcome of its initiatives.

Bank of America's Private Bank 2026 Study of Wealthy Americans (published 2026-06-17) covers Gen Z and Millennials aged 21 to 45. It reports that 67% believe traditional stocks and bonds can no longer deliver above-average returns, and 88% say they are likely to allocate more to alternatives in the next few years (vs. 15% of Boomers and Silents). It also reports that 32% of Gen Z and Millennials have a prenuptial agreement, vs. 15% of Gen X and 4% of Boomers and Silents, and says planning is starting earlier among younger married investors.
UBS (published 2026-04-22) reports that most next-generation respondents (83%) favor a blended approach to communicating, combining digital convenience with in-person interaction.

Schwab's Q3 2025 call (published 2025-10-16) says one-third of retail households that created a financial plan within the last two years are under the age of 40. Management says the average age of its clients continues to get younger.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) names, as a risk, changing client expectations for expanded product offerings and technology needs, and changing client demographics, preferences and values. It also names competition from firms offering enhanced digital experiences and lower-cost computer-based "robo-advice", and says clients can transfer their business to competitors at any time.

UBS's next-generation study (published 2026-04-22) reports that when succession planning involves private banking partners, 41% prefer to work with their family's existing bank, 31% want a new provider and 29% are open to switching. UBS's respondents are next-generation members of wealthy families.

Edward Jones's 10-Qs for the second quarter (published 2025-08-08) and third quarter (published 2025-11-07) of 2025 attribute elevated asset outflows partly to an aging client base and generational wealth transfers outside the firm. The Q2 filing says the net new asset decrease was attributable to existing clients.
Morgan Stanley's CEO said on the 4Q24 call (published 2025-01-16) that the firm retains 99% of its clients. This is not split by age or by inheritance.

Schwab's CEO said on the 3Q26 call (published 2026-10-15) that its retention rate around wealth transfers is extremely high. The accompanying deck (published 2026-10-15) shows about 75% of assets retained in a wealth transfer event. These are management's own figures.

Cerulli (published 2025-10-29) says notable differences in service preferences among women and next-generation clients are likely to shift market share to the firms best prepared to meet their needs. It warns advisors of the risks that wealth transfers pose to their practices.

adjacent.text: Wealthtender's advisor-search survey (published 2025-08-13) found that 97% plan to interview multiple advisors and 96% will do further research online before hiring. It found 83% research the advisor's reputation through online reviews and awards, and 64% want to know the advisor's areas of specialization and 62% the fee/pricing structure before making contact. Among sources people use to find advisors, the survey lists AI search tools (25.40%), social media (22.20%), online advisor directories (31.80%), financial institutions (49.00%) and referrals from professionals (49.20%).

claims.text: Size and timing - Cerulli (research published 2025-10-29): Cerulli projects households will transfer $123.7 trillion to heirs ($105 trillion) and charities ($18 trillion) between now and 2048. It says wealth is now more likely to be held by older households.

Gen X, millennials and women - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Generation Xers are expected to inherit $39 trillion and Millennials $46 trillion. Women in the Baby Boomer and older generations are expected to receive $40 trillion in 'horizontal' transfers as they outlive their husbands. Women in younger generations are expected to receive $47 trillion of the wealth transferred intergenerationally.

Nature of the transfer - Cerulli (published 2025-10-29): Cerulli says most of the wealth owned by older generations will eventually be donated or passed to Gen X or Millennial heirs, an estimated total of $85 trillion. Its 2024 Private Wealth Management Executive Survey lists the top factors preventing HNW wealth transfer planning. Two are 'not comfortable sharing financial information with their children' (64%) and 'fear that children are not prepared to inherit wealth' (64%). Two more are 'inexperience with multi-generational wealth strategies' (56%) and 'clients are unwilling to give up control to the next generation' (44%).

Global view - UBS report (published 2026-04-22): UBS estimates USD 83 trillion in private wealth will change hands globally over the next two to three decades (foreword) and about two decades (introduction). It describes the transfer as a journey that unfolds over time, not a single event. This is a global estimate, a different scope from Cerulli's household figures.

claims.text: Definition of net new assets - Morgan Stanley: the 3Q26 supplement (published 2026-10-14) and press release say net new assets represent client asset inflows, including interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, and exclude the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions. The 2025 10-K uses the same wording and adds that NNA is influenced by factors such as macro conditions, seasonality, advisor and client retention and large idiosyncratic inflows and outflows including single large client events.
claims.source_label: MS supplement 2026-09-30, p.15 [IR]; MS press - Wealth Management segment 2026-09-30 [filing]; MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]

claims.text: Definition of net new assets - Schwab: Schwab's headline metric is core net new assets. A note in the 3Q26 deck (2026-10-15) defines it as net new assets before significant one-time flows, such as acquisitions/divestitures or extraordinary flows (generally greater than $25 billion; $10 billion in prior periods) relating to a specific client, and activity from off-platform Schwab Bank Retail CDs; these flows may span multiple reporting periods.

Definition of net new assets - Schwab: Schwab's 2Q26 press release (2026-07-21) notes that, unless otherwise noted, differences between net new assets and core net new assets are net flows from off-platform Schwab Bank Retail CDs. The 2025 10-K glossary (published 2026-02-25) defines 'net new client assets' as total inflows of client cash and securities to Schwab less client outflows, where inflows include dividends and interest, outflows include commissions and fees, and capital gains distributions are excluded.

Definition of net new assets - Edward Jones: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states that net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.

Definition of net new assets - Edward Jones: the 2026 10-Qs (1Q26 published 2026-05-07; 2Q26 published 2026-08-07) state that net new assets represents cash and securities inflows and outflows, including fees and commissions and excluding mutual fund capital gain distributions received by U.S. clients.

Definition of net new assets - Raymond James: its supplement (published 2026-07-22) and press release say Domestic Private Client Group net new assets represents domestic PCG client inflows, including dividends and interest, less domestic PCG client outflows, including commissions, advisory fees and other fees. The annualized growth percentage is based on the beginning domestic PCG assets under administration balance for the period. The measure covers the domestic PCG only.
claims.source_label: RJF supplement 2026-06-30, p.18 [IR]; RJF press - Private Client Group segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Total client assets - Morgan Stanley: The Wealth Management financial supplement (published 2026-10-14) shows total client assets of $8,433 billion at September 30, 2026, of which advisor-led client assets were $6,631 billion. claims.text: Total client assets - Schwab: The 3Q26 earnings release (published 2026-10-15) shows total client assets of 13,333.2 ($ billions) at the end of the quarter, split into Investor Services 7,487.3 and Advisor Services 5,845.9. The prior-quarter column (June 30, 2026) shows 13,084.9 total. On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), the CEO said the adviser business serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets.

Total client assets - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) reports client assets under care of $2,647 billion at period end (June 26, 2026), including advisory programs of $1,198 billion.

claims.text: Financial advisor count - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) states the Partnership ended the second quarter of 2026 with 20,514 financial advisors. The segment table splits the period-end count into 19,647 and 867 across its two geographic columns (the firm operates in the U.S. and Canada).

Financial advisor count - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (period ending 2025-09-30) reports 8,943 total advisors, made up of 3,878 employees and 5,065 independent contractors. Advisors in the RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division are not included in the count.

Definitions - Morgan Stanley: Wealth Management defines client assets as covering advisor-led brokerage, investment advisory, custody and related services, self-directed brokerage and advisory services, financial and wealth planning, and workplace services including stock plan administration and retirement plan services. Advisor-led client assets are those in accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned. Self-directed client assets are active accounts that are not advisor-led, with active meaning at least $25 in assets. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) says stock plan unvested assets are not included in client assets. The 3Q26 supplement shows advisor-led client assets of $6,631 billion and self-directed client assets of $1,802 billion within total client assets of $8,433 billion.

claims.text: Definitions - Schwab: Schwab's 2025 10-K describes two segments. Investor Services covers retail brokerage, advisory and banking and trust services to individuals, plus retirement plan and business services. Advisor Services provides custodial, trading, banking and trust, and support services to independent RIAs, independent retirement advisors and recordkeepers. Schwab defines assets receiving ongoing advisory services as client assets custodied at the company under the guidance of an independent advisor or enrolled in one of Schwab's managed investing solutions. Schwab Advisor Network advisors are described as independent and not employees or agents of Charles Schwab & Co. Total client assets of 13,333.2 ($ billions) include 5,845.9 in Advisor Services.
claims.source_label: SCHW 10-K 2025-12-31 [filing]; SCHW deck 2026-05-14, p.186 [IR]; SCHW press 2026-09-30 [filing]

claims.text: Definitions - Edward Jones: The 2Q26 10-Q describes 'client assets under care' for the Partnership, which operates in the U.S. and Canada, and the advisor count covers both countries. The 2025 10-K risk factors note that many of the Partnership's financial advisors are employees. Client assets under care of $2,647 billion are reported on a consolidated basis for the Partnership.

Definitions - Merrill: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business as a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets. No Merrill-specific definition of an advisor count or of client assets is in the evidence; see the adjacent GWIM items.

Definitions - Raymond James: The FY2025 10-K (period ending 2025-09-30) says its AUA includes assets of firms affiliated through RCS ($217.3 billion at September 30, 2025), while financial advisors associated with RCS firms are not in the financial advisor counts. Its advisor count combines employee advisors and independent contractor advisors. The 10-K says independent contractor advisors are responsible for their direct costs and receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors. The firm reports client assets under administration of $1,922.4 billion, of which PCG AUA is $1,856.5 billion. The 3Q FY26 release says Clark Capital ($47 billion of total client assets at acquisition) was integrated into the Asset Management segment.

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that for certain revenue-producing employees in Wealth Management and Investment Management, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link compensation to revenues. It gives no payout percentages in the cited text.

Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley (deferred pay): The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that the Firm sponsors deferred cash-based and stock-based compensation programs including for Wealth Management financial advisors, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions. Advisor deferred compensation is generally 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) repeats this language.
claims.source_label: MS 10-K - Wealth Management segment 2025-12-31 [filing]; MS 10-Q - Wealth Management segment 2026-06-30 [filing]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley (deferred pay accounting): The 1Q26 10-Q (published 2026-05-05) says DCP compensation expense is based on the notional award value adjusted for changes in the fair value of the investments employees select, and is recognized over the vesting period. Beginning in 1Q26 the Firm hedges certain DCP awards with derivatives and no longer presents non-GAAP measures excluding DCP (1Q26 earnings release, 2026-04-15).
claims.source_label: MS 10-Q 2026-03-31 [filing]; MS press - Wealth Management segment 2026-03-31 [filing]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Morgan Stanley (conflicts disclosure): Morgan Stanley's Form ADV (published 2026-11-04) states that Financial Advisors and their Branch Managers receive no additional compensation from the fund-related payments Morgan Stanley receives.

Advisor compensation structure - Merrill: Merrill's Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) says the advisor compensation structure creates conflicts of interest. It says advisors earn compensation based on revenue Merrill earns from the Merrill Lynch Fee in the Program, on other fees and costs, on Sales Charges in brokerage accounts, and on referrals to Affiliates including banking products.

Advisor compensation structure - Merrill (awards): Merrill's Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) says advisors are eligible for a compensation award, payable over a defined period, from an incentive program currently based on meeting prior-year growth targets in new households and in assets and liabilities. An advisor is subject to a reduction in their incentive compensation grid if they fail to achieve growth in assets and liabilities for two consecutive years. The ADV says Merrill approves its compensation program year to year and the criteria can change. Advisors receive no additional compensation for advisory client assets held in the Cash Sweep Program.

Advisor compensation structure - Merrill (management pay): Merrill's Form ADV (published 2026-10-30) says field management compensation is based partly on revenues to Merrill and on advisors meeting strategic goals, and that management incentive compensation reflects the profitability of Merrill and BofA Corp. Merrill itself acknowledges a resulting conflict of interest.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes a firm-wide employee compensation package of base pay plus performance-based incentive pay, equity awards, recognition awards and benefits. This text is not specific to financial consultants or advisors.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab (financial consultants): Schwab Wealth Advisory's Form ADV (published 2026-10-15) says financial consultants (FCs) receive compensation for enrolling clients in the SWA Program and for ongoing service, and that this varies by program or service chosen. Schwab acknowledges FCs may earn more on SWA assets than on commission-based brokerage accounts or certain other advisory programs, a potential conflict of interest. It points to schwab.com/representative-compensation for more.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab (bonus and incentive): The 3Q26 deck (published 2026-10-15) says Schwab uses adjusted diluted EPS and return on tangible common equity as performance criteria for employee bonus and certain executive incentive arrangements, with Compensation Committee discretion. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) attributes higher incentive compensation to the Company's financial performance and notes headcount growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors.

Advisor compensation structure - Schwab (referral-based): The investor-day deck (published 2026-05-14) states that Schwab Advisor Network advisors are independent, not Schwab employees, and pay fees to Schwab in connection with referrals. This is the advisor paying Schwab, not Schwab paying its own advisors.

Advisor compensation structure - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states that financial advisors are generally compensated on a commission basis, subject to a minimum guaranteed salary. It says they may be entitled to additional compensation based on branch office profitability and the Partnership's profitability. The retirement plan consists of a profit-sharing contribution tied to the Partnership's profitability and a 401(k) contribution.

Advisor compensation structure - Edward Jones (variable pay): The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) says a significant portion of the Partnership's profits is allocated to variable compensation paid to associates as bonuses and profit sharing, a key component of its performance-based compensation model. It reports variable compensation up 33% in the quarter to $780 and 27% in the first half to $1,528, due to increased branch and Firm profitability.

Advisor compensation structure - Edward Jones (referrals and conflicts): Edward Jones's Form ADV (published 2026-03-27) says Edward Jones and its financial advisors pay third parties for client referrals and leads (paid solicitor arrangements), using flat or subscription fees or ongoing fees as a percentage of advisory program fees. It also says revenue sharing creates additional financial benefits to the firm, its financial advisors and equity owners.
claims.source_label: EDJ adv 2026-03-27, p.22 [filing]; EDJ adv 2026-03-27, p.21 [filing]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (payout ranges): Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists payout by affiliation model: Traditional Employee up to 50%; Advisor Select 70-80% gross payout; Independent Contractor 81% to 90%; Corporate RIA 81% to 90%. For Bank & Credit Union it describes a compensation package from the financial institution, and for RIA & Custody Services compensation is set with the RIA or broker/dealer.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (employee vs independent contractor): On the fiscal 2Q26 call (published 2026-04-22), CEO Paul Shoukry said independent payouts are higher because independent advisors cover their own overhead, real estate and health insurance. He said even the employee side has tiered payout systems, so higher production moves an advisor up the payout grid. Raymond James's Advisor Select page (content as of 2026-03-11) says advisors who run their branch's P&L earn a higher rate on production.
claims.source_label: RJF transcript 2026-03-31 [IR]; RJF press page content as of 2026-03-11 [IR]

claims.text: Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (Form ADV): Raymond James's Form ADV (published 2026-09-14) says an advisor's share of the advisory fee can rise with annual revenue generation, and that advisors may share part of their payout with other advisors. Newly affiliated advisors in the Advisor Mastery Program may receive a salary in addition to advisory fees (or in addition to commissions and trails) for a period of time.

Advisor compensation structure - Raymond James (retention awards): On the fiscal 4Q25 call (published 2025-10-22), the CFO said fiscal 2025 adjusted compensation expense included amortization of transition assistance for recruited advisors and other retention awards to existing advisors totaling $355 million, up approximately 11% from fiscal 2024.

claims.text: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-11-12) reports Raymond James will add $18.7 billion and 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp., expanding its relationship with Pinnacle Financial Partners; the advisors are expected to transition in May 2027. FID president Stephen Kruchten called it "a significant and highly strategic expansion" of the relationship.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-06) reports Raymond James & Associates (RJA), the employee advisor channel, landed a Washington, D.C. team (KKM Wealth Partners within Alex. Brown) from PNC Private Bank that managed over $1.5 billion in client assets; the article adds that RJA had announced a $700 million team earlier that week, the second in as many weeks at that size.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-06) also reports that Ameriprise welcomed back Ricardo Baptiste, who has $193 million in client assets, after a six-year stint at Raymond James (a departure from Raymond James).

InvestmentNews (2026-11-05) reports two Virginia advisors (Mintz & Gow Group) joined RJA from Truist Investment Services with more than $1.2 billion in client assets. The article says Raymond James ended its fiscal year with a record 8,943 advisors, up 2% year-over-year, and has signaled it expects continued momentum with healthy pipelines of advisor commitments. This conflicts with WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29), which says Raymond James no longer reports advisor headcount and had about 8,900 advisors when it last broke it out.
claims.source_label: RJF trade 2026-11-05 [trade press (indicative only)]; RJF trade 2026-10-29 [trade press (indicative only)]

claims.text: InvestmentNews (2026-11-05) says the Richmond hire is the latest in a sustained Raymond James recruitment drive, citing earlier-in-the-year teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley and a $420 million Edward Jones team in Virginia late last year.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-04) reports RJA welcomed a four-advisor team from UBS Financial Services in Beachwood, Ohio (42° North Advisors of Raymond James) that managed more than $700 million; the team cited Raymond James's reputation, stability and leadership as deciding factors.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29), reporting on the fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call, says Raymond James reported record quarter-end client assets under administration of $1.87 trillion, up 1% sequentially and 12% year-over-year. The Private Client Group had record quarterly net revenue of $3.06 billion, up 15% year-over-year, and pre-tax income of $458 million, up 10% year-over-year.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reports domestic PCG net new assets rose 88% for the fiscal year to a record of more than $98 billion; quarterly net new assets were nearly $23 billion, with annualized growth from the beginning of the quarter of 5.3%.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-29) reports non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.59, which it says beat analysts' expectations by $0.32 according to Seeking Alpha, on revenue of $4.74 billion, up 13% year-over-year.

On the fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call (reported 2026-10-29), CEO Paul Shoukry said trailing 12-month production for recruited advisors entering the domestic independent contractor and employee channels was $538 million, up from $407 million the prior year, representing more than $82 billion in client assets. He said recruiting success spans all affiliation channels, including RIA custody, with the independent contractor channel seeing the most interest in dollar volume.

On M&A (reported 2026-10-29), Shoukry said the firm looks for wealth management acquisitions in particular, but they must be a good cultural and strategic fit: "We don't do acquisitions to slash costs... We do acquisitions to grow revenues and to be better firms together over time."

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-23) reports Raymond James recruited a Southwest Florida team managing about $700 million from Truist Investment Services into its Financial Institutions Division (via Pinnacle Asset Management); it describes FID as established in 1987 and serving about 950 advisors across 160 institutions.

Departure: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-16) reports Janney Montgomery Scott is opening a Houston office seeded by the Edward Fitzpatrick Group, which had been with Raymond James about 23 years and amassed $3.3 billion in client assets, plus an advisor overseeing more than $200 million.

Departure: WealthManagement.com (2026-10-08) reports four practices with more than $1 billion in client assets left Raymond James Financial Services for Ascentis Independent Advisors, an RIA platform, and will continue to use Raymond James as their primary custodian.

InvestmentNews and WealthManagement.com (2026-09-29) report Raymond James launched Private Wealth Guided Portfolios, a risk-based model framework combining equity and fixed income with a dedicated alternatives sleeve (private markets and hedged strategies) for advisors serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients. PCG President Tash Elwyn said the firm is "committed to being a destination for private wealth advisors." Asset Management Services builds the models with the Private Markets and Alternatives team.

InvestmentNews (2026-09-29) reports nearly 450 advisors have earned the Raymond James Private Wealth Advisor designation (launched September 2022) as of September 2026. It also recounts that Raymond James agreed in January 2026 to acquire Clark Capital Management Group (more than $46 billion under management), which closed in May 2026 and joined Raymond James Investment Management as an independent boutique.

InvestmentNews (2026-09-29) notes that Shoukry has emphasized building advisory ranks through individualized one-on-one recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, and that the firm is piloting an AI-powered advisor assistant called Raimond.

WealthManagement.com and InvestmentNews (2026-09-24) report Raymond James added a $1.25 billion Iowa team (Greenwood Wealth Partners, from D.M. Kelly) to its employee channel and a $500 million Rochester, N.Y. team (Harris Wealth Partners, from Commonwealth Financial Network) to its independent channel. WealthManagement.com says Raymond James has been one of the most significant beneficiaries of teams leaving Commonwealth ahead of its LPL conversion and has boosted recruitment spending over the past year, according to earnings reports.

WealthManagement.com (2026-09-16) reports, citing a regulatory filing and a spokesperson, that Raymond James made a firm-wide SIMPLE IRA Employer Advisory and Consulting Services Program, partnered with Capital Group American Funds, available to its roughly 8,900 advisors for small businesses with up to 100 employees.
InvestmentNews (2026-09-02) reports RJA added a team from UBS Financial Services in The Woodlands, Texas (Le Sage Mattiza Maggard Wealth Management) that previously managed more than $550 million.

InvestmentNews (2026-08-26) reports Jeffrey Stillwell, with approximately $240 million from Ameriprise Financial Services, affiliated with Raymond James Financial Services in Red Bank, New Jersey, citing investment banking access and lending solutions for business-owner clients.

InvestmentNews (2026-08-21) reports RJA welcomed Adam Pearsall from UBS, who managed more than $400 million, in Glens Falls, New York; a division director cited continued investment in the Capital Region.
InvestmentNews (2026-08-19) reports Raymond James Financial Services welcomed Roberto De Jesus from Edward Jones after 18 years, with approximately $199 million in client assets, in Acworth, Georgia.

claims.text: AdvisorHub trade press (2026-11-16; indicative only) reports a private wealth team managing $1 billion at UBS Wealth Management USA joined Merrill in Boston, in the Northeast private wealth unit led by Nathan Marsden. A spokesperson for Merrill confirmed the move.

AdvisorHub (2026-11-16; indicative only) reports Franklin J. Laden joined Merrill in Denver from UBS with $375 million in assets. It also says Merrill added an advisor managing $205 million from Morgan Stanley and one overseeing $150 million from Edward D. Jones that month. It says Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting.

AdvisorHub (2026-11-16; indicative only) says Merrill largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 and returned under Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023. It says they restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. This is the leadership context the evidence gives; it does not show a leadership change in 2026.

InvestmentNews (2026-11-12; indicative only) reports Jonathan Stogsdill, a Merrill vice president and financial solutions advisor of more than eight years, joined Trinity Wealth Advisors, an RIA. It also notes that in March 2026 Cyndeo Wealth Partners added a Merrill veteran with roughly $235 million in client assets.

WealthManagement.com (2026-11-03; indicative only) reports JPMorgan hired Tiffany Yu, registered with Merrill since 1998, to join a Los Angeles J.P. Morgan Advisors team. She manages about $940 million. JPMorgan also hired another Merrill alum, Linda Patel, as Southeast Regional Director.

In the 3Q26 supplement (2026-10-14), Bank of America reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5,905 million in 3Q26 and $5,261 million in 3Q25. It reports Merrill Wealth Management client balances of $4,240,601 million at 30 September 2026, against $3,815,389 million at 31 March 2026 and $3,992,312 million at 31 December 2025.

In the 3Q26 earnings release (2026-10-14), Bank of America lists these Merrill Wealth Management highlights: $4.2 trillion in client balances, $1.9 trillion in AUM balances, ~4.2K net new $500K+ households added in 3Q26, and 70K digital appointments scheduled in the quarter. It also lists 87% of Merrill households digitally active, up from 86% in the 4Q25 release.
claims.source_label: BAC press - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [filing]; BAC press - GWIM segment 2025-12-31 [filing]

claims.text: On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. He said 67% of Merrill clients now have banking relationships with Bank of America. He credited advisor productivity, disciplined pricing, digital engagement and AI tools, and said the results reflect the firm's ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.

On the 3Q26 call with reporters (2026-10-14, as reported by InvestmentNews; indicative only), Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management, said client sales of alternative investments at Merrill increased 19% in the quarter. The article says the message was that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities. It notes Schimpf did not mention new AI tools.

InvestmentNews (2026-10-14; indicative only) reports Nick Economos launched Economos Private Wealth through LPL's independent advisor network, bringing approximately $580 million in advisory and brokerage assets from Merrill Lynch.

InvestmentNews (2026-10-16; indicative only) reports Merrill and Wells Fargo agreed to a combined $4.4 million settlement with state securities regulators over unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions. Merrill faces restitution on approximately $549,000 in excess commissions from September 30, 2020 through October 1, 2025.

WealthManagement.com (2026-10-15; indicative only) reports both Wells Fargo entities and Merrill Lynch must pay administrative fines and costs. They must also verify they have changed policies and procedures so commissions are "fair and reasonable". A Merrill spokesperson said the firm "addressed the issues raised in the settlement several years ago."

InvestmentNews (2026-10-02; indicative only) reports Merrill agreed to pay $39 million to settle a class action alleging it paid close-to-zero interest on cash in retirement accounts. This is on top of the $25 million SEC penalty from January 2025, for a combined $64 million. A separate report in the same coverage says the settlement covers Merrill Edge account holders between December 15, 2016 and March 15, 2020, and that Merrill denied wrongdoing.

RIABiz (2026-09-29; indicative only) reports Merrill created new data-analytics fees and a revenue-share "support fee" for third-party asset managers, effective Jan. 1, 2027, and disclosed in its Form ADV. Data fees on actively managed products run $125,000 to $860,000 per firm per year. The support fee is negotiable and runs from 0.02% up to 0.1% on certain third-party funds. Merrill's filing says it will have a financial incentive to recommend products from firms that pay for data analytics.

A Merrill press release (2026-09-15) announced two new services in the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program: a Tax Efficient Transition Service and a Dollar Cost Averaging Service. Both are optional, with no additional IAP Program Fees charged, and are implemented by Managed Account Advisors LLC. Merrill's Jay Link described them as helping clients stay focused on long-term goals.

WealthManagement.com (2026-09-11 and 2026-09-08; indicative only) reports a flurry of Merrill recruiting wins. These include a $1.2 billion UBS team in Santa Fe, N.M., and a $1.2 billion Morgan Stanley team in McLean, Va. They also include advisors from Truist and Wells Fargo, for combined wins of $1.8 billion in the earlier report. The articles say Merrill is ramping up advisor recruiting.

claims.text: The Bank of America 2Q26 10-Q (2026-07-31) reports Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5.7 billion, up 16%, for the quarter and $11.3 billion, up 13%, for six months. It attributes this to higher asset management fees (market valuations and positive AUM flows) and higher brokerage fees. The 2Q26 supplement shows $5,711 million versus $4,942 million in 2Q25.

In the 2Q26 release (2026-07-14), Bank of America lists these Merrill Wealth Management highlights: $4.1 trillion in client balances, $1.8 trillion in AUM balances, and ~5.4K net new $500K+ households added in 2Q26. claims.text: On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-14), CFO Borthwick described the Merrill growth target as aiming for 5% over the next 3 to 5 years and said "we're off to a good start." He said Lindsay [Hans], Eric [Schimpf] and Katy are trying to keep growing the sales force, and that adviser attrition is "now at near historic lows." He also said both Merrill and the Private Bank continued to attract talented advisers, and cited new AI-enabled tools that help advisers prepare for client conversations.

The Bank of America 1Q26 10-Q (2026-05-01) says Merrill Wealth Management revenue of $5.6 billion increased 11%. It cites higher asset management fees and higher brokerage fees, partially offset by the impact of lower AUM pricing. The 1Q26 supplement shows $5,579 million versus $5,019 million in 1Q25.

In the 1Q26 release (2026-04-15), Bank of America cites Merrill recognitions. These include the most recognitions on Forbes' 2026 Best-in-State Wealth Management Teams list (32 teams ranked No. 1), more than 300 advisors on Barron's 2026 Top 1,500, and No. 1 in Managed Personal Trust AUM. On the 1Q26 call, Borthwick said the firm remained focused on pricing discipline, adviser productivity and continuing to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

claims.text: Edward Jones defines its attrition metric as the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end (10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-09-26, published 2025-11-07).
In its second-quarter 2025 10-Q (published 2025-08-08), Edward Jones said financial advisor attrition increased to 6.4%, primarily due to an increase in retirements, consistent with industry trends.

In its third-quarter 2025 10-Q (published 2025-11-07), Edward Jones reported financial advisor attrition of 6.1% versus 4.7% in the third quarter of 2024, and 6.0% for the nine months versus 5.1% a year earlier. It attributed the quarter to a variety of factors, including a rise in departures among advisors with tenure of five years or less.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) names attrition as a risk. It states there is no assurance the Partnership can grow, retain, develop and support its financial advisors, and no assurance that past attrition rates will not increase. It says lower Firm profitability and revenue could increase attrition. It also says advisor attrition could rise if product offerings or the employment model do not meet advisor expectations.

On the 2Q26 earnings call (2026-07-14), Bank of America's CFO, discussing the Merrill growth guide, said adviser attrition is now at near historic lows. No numeric Merrill attrition rate is given in the evidence.

Edward Jones's 10-Q for the second quarter of 2025 (published 2025-08-08) shows 20,309 financial advisors at period end versus 19,589 a year earlier (+4%). The 10-Q for the third quarter of 2025 (published 2025-11-07) says the Partnership ended the quarter with 20,429 financial advisors.

The Edward Jones 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership relies heavily on referrals from its current financial advisors to recruit new advisors. It says it has been, and may continue to be, more difficult to attract qualified applicants in volatile markets, and that new advisors may struggle to build their businesses.

On the 2Q25 call (2025-07-16), Bank of America's CFO said the firm continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through its training program and experienced hiring. He said about one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by newly trained advisors.

On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-14), the CFO said Merrill FAs see the value of the franchise and the firm is picking up recruiting of experienced advisors. He described this as not an enormous part of the strategy, alongside a training program.

On the 1Q26 call (2026-04-15), the CFO said the firm continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers. On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), he said Merrill results reflect the firm's ability to attract clients and experienced advisers to the platform.
claims.source_label: BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-03-31 [IR]; BAC transcript - GWIM segment 2026-09-30 [IR]

It says the count includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that for certain revenue-producing employees in Wealth Management and Investment Management, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.

The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that Morgan Stanley sponsors deferred cash-based and stock-based compensation programs that include Wealth Management financial advisors, and that these generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions. It says deferred compensation for Wealth Management financial advisors is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards. Employees can allocate deferred cash awards among a firm-selected menu of notional investments (fixed income, equity, commodity and money market funds).

The June 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) repeats the 75% cash / 25% stock composition of Wealth Management advisor deferred compensation. It says compensation expense for deferred cash awards is based on the notional award value, adjusted for changes in the fair value of the investments employees select, and is recognized over the vesting period.

The 3Q26 financial supplement (published 2026-10-14) says that beginning in the first quarter of 2026, hedges for Wealth Management deferred cash-based compensation awards were primarily transitioned to derivative instruments. As a result, the firm no longer presents non-GAAP measures of net revenues and compensation expense excluding DCP.

adjacent.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) reports firm-wide compensation and benefits expense of $29,216 million in 2025, up 12%. It attributes the rise primarily to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors and higher discretionary incentive compensation within Institutional Securities, both on higher revenues, and to higher salary expenses.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: The June 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) says Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses increased primarily as a result of an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenues. No payout rate is given.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (published 2026-10-26) reported that Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay. It also reported that Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses in their 2027 pay plans. The article describes large firms like Morgan Stanley as having taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation that advisors must stay for years to vest, with forfeiture on departure.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews (published 2026-08-28) reported that Morgan Stanley sued a former advisor in 2021 over promissory notes (loans brokers pay back to firms over time) and sought to claw back recruiting bonus money. This indicates that recruiting bonuses exist, but it gives no terms.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

gaps.what: Payout grids are not public. The evidence gives no payout percentages or grid tiers, no commission or fee-based payout rates, no bonus amounts, and no average or aggregate advisor pay figures for Morgan Stanley Wealth Management.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley Wealth Management advisor compensation plan documents or recruiting disclosures; industry compensation surveys

adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.
